Managing citations in R Markdown and Quarto

Source: vignettes/citation-management.Rmd
citation-management.Rmd

R Markdown (.Rmd) and Quarto (.qmd) use Pandoc to turn citation keys into formatted citations and a reference list. The two formats use the same BibTeX bibliography files, citation syntax, and Citation Style Language (CSL) files.

Create a BibTeX bibliography

Store references in a plain-text file with a .bib extension. Each entry has a type, a unique citation key, and fields describing the source. For example, save the following as references.bib next to your manuscript:

@article{wickham2014,
  author  = {Wickham, Hadley},
  title   = {Tidy Data},
  journal = {Journal of Statistical Software},
  year    = {2014},
  volume  = {59},
  number  = {10},
  pages   = {1--23},
  doi     = {10.18637/jss.v059.i10}
}

@book{xie2018,
  author    = {Xie, Yihui and Allaire, J. J. and Grolemund, Garrett},
  title     = {R Markdown: The Definitive Guide},
  publisher = {Chapman and Hall/CRC},
  year      = {2018},
  url       = {https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/}
}

@misc{quarto2026,
  author = {{Posit Software, PBC}},
  title  = {Quarto Documentation},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://quarto.org/docs/}
}

The citation keys in this example are wickham2014, xie2018, and quarto2026. Reference managers such as Zotero can export an entire library or a selected collection as BibTeX.

Connect the bibliography to a document

Add the bibliography path to the document’s YAML header. The path is relative to the .Rmd or .qmd file.

For an R Markdown manuscript:

---
title: "My manuscript"
output: word_document
bibliography: references.bib
---

For a Quarto manuscript:

---
title: "My manuscript"
format: docx
bibliography: references.bib
---

Both formats also accept multiple bibliography files:

bibliography:
  - references.bib
  - software.bib

Cite sources in the text

Use the entry’s citation key after an @:

Wickham (@wickham2014) describes a consistent structure for tidy data.

R Markdown supports reproducible manuscripts [@xie2018].

Several tools support this workflow [@xie2018; @quarto2026].

The relevant discussion appears in a specific section [@xie2018, sec. 2.8].

These forms produce narrative, parenthetical, multiple, and located citations, respectively. The first two forms render in this vignette as follows: Wickham (Wickham (2014)) describes a consistent structure for tidy data, and R Markdown supports reproducible manuscripts (Xie et al. 2018).

Pandoc creates the reference list from cited entries. To include every entry from the bibliography, even if it is not cited, add this YAML option:

nocite: |
  @*

Choose a citation style

A CSL file controls details such as citation order, punctuation, and whether citations use author–date text or numbers. Download a style from the CSL style repository and save it with the manuscript. Then add its path to the same YAML header:

bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl

The YAML is identical in .Rmd and .qmd files. If csl is omitted, Pandoc uses its default author–date style.

The CSL repository includes thousands of journal and publisher styles. Common starting points include:

  • APA (apa.csl) for author–date citations;
  • Elsevier - Vancouver (elsevier-vancouver.csl) for numbered biomedical citations;
  • Chicago author-date (chicago-author-date.csl);
  • Nature (nature.csl) for numbered citations; and
  • IEEE (ieee.csl) for bracketed numeric citations.

Use the repository’s file search to find a journal-specific style. Download the raw .csl file rather than saving the GitHub HTML page. Keeping the .bib and .csl files under version control with the manuscript makes the rendered references reproducible for collaborators.

References

Wickham, Hadley. 2014. “Tidy Data.” Journal of Statistical Software 59 (10): 1–23. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v059.i10.
Xie, Yihui, J. J. Allaire, and Garrett Grolemund. 2018. R Markdown: The Definitive Guide. Chapman; Hall/CRC. https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/.
